title: Maximum Subarray / Kadane's Algorithm: running sum, reset when negative.
shortTitle: Maximum Subarray / Kadane's Algorithm: Running Sum, Reset When Negative
keyPoints: Kadane's Algorithm finds the contiguous subarray with the largest sum in a single O(n) pass with O(1) extra space.
At each element, take the larger of extending the running sum or starting fresh, then update the global best.
When the running sum drops below the current element alone, carrying the past forward only hurts, so you reset.
Initialize both currentBest and globalBest to the first element so an all-negative array returns the least negative value, not zero.
Track a tentative start index that resets on each fresh start, and record start and end when globalBest improves, to recover the actual subarray.
Use BigDecimal for money sums so amounts stay exact across the entire running total.
This is a dynamic-programming idea: the optimal subarray ending at position i depends only on the optimal subarray ending at position i minus one.

s1_definition.oneliner: At each element take the larger of extending the run or starting new, and track the best run seen.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Kadane's Algorithm** – solves the Maximum Subarray problem by finding the contiguous slice of an array with the largest sum in a single linear pass.
- **Running best-ending-here** – at each index `i`, `currentBest = Math.max(a[i], currentBest + a[i])` decides whether to extend or restart.
- **Global best** – `globalBest = Math.max(globalBest, currentBest)` captures the highest running sum seen at any position.
- **O(n) time, O(1) space** – the algorithm touches each element exactly once and uses only two extra variables.
- **All-negative safety** – initializing both values to `a[0]` ensures the answer is the least negative element, not zero, when every element is negative.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India lists Rajesh's daily net cash flow, positive on credit days and negative on debit days, and an analyst wants the single stretch of consecutive days that produced the largest total gain. Walking day by day, you keep a running tally, but the moment carrying the past forward would drag you down below just starting fresh today, you reset and start a new stretch from today. You always remember the best stretch total you have ever seen.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Maximum Subarray asks for the contiguous slice of an array with the largest sum, and Kadane's Algorithm solves it in a single linear pass with constant space. You keep a running best-ending-here sum and a global best. At each element you take the larger of the element alone or the element added to the previous running sum. When carrying the past forward would only hurt, the element alone wins and the run effectively resets, and you update the global best each step.

The reset-when-negative intuition is the core. If the sum you have been carrying ever drops below what you would get by starting fresh at the current element, that past baggage can only shrink any future sum, so you throw it away and begin a new run. That single local decision at each element is why the whole problem collapses from a quadratic search over all slices to one linear scan.

The edge case to always call out is an all-negative array. The answer must be the least negative single element, not zero, so you initialize both the running and global best to the first element rather than to zero, which would wrongly allow an empty subarray. You also track a tentative start index so you can report the actual start and end days of the winning stretch, and you use BigDecimal with add and compareTo so every sum is exact.

In a banking project at the National Bank of India, Rajesh's daily net cash flow is scanned to find the single consecutive stretch of days that produced his largest total net gain, even when some months are entirely negative. Explaining the extend-or-reset decision, the all-negative initialization, and the index tracking shows the interviewer that you understand Kadane's as a dynamic-programming idea, not a memorized trick.

Remember one sentence: Kadane's Algorithm keeps a running sum at each element, resets when extending would hurt, and tracks the global best, solving Maximum Subarray in O(n) time and O(1) space.
